newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Jollibee to raise at least 1.5 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Jollibee to raise at least 1.5 bln pesos.

text.p: Jollibee Foods Corp, the leader in the Philippines' fastfood sector, said on Wednesday it plans to raise funds of at least 1.5 billion pesos in domestic capital markets in this quarter.
Raffy de la Rosa, the company's chief finance officer, said during an analysts' briefing the company is looking at issuing new shares or warrants, or offering a convertible bond.
"We may raise at least 1.5 billion pesos to cover for this year and next year," he said.
The new shares that may be sold will comprise about nine percent of expanded capital, he said. The public currently owns 21 percent of Jollibee.
"There is enough leeway to raise more equity," de la Rosa added.

If the company decides to sell warrants, foreign investors may be able to have an exposure in Jollibee, he said. Existing laws currently bar foreign investors from a direct stake in companies engaged in domestic retail trade.
The new funds will settle short-term loans and partly fund the company's expansion programme, he said.
Jollibee is set to undertake expansion programmes worth 1.0 billion to 1.3 billion pesos this year compared with more than 1.1 billion pesos last year, he said.

The company's net profit could rise by 20 percent to 30 percent this year, de la Rosa said. In 1996, the company reported a 12 percent increase in net income to 603 million pesos from 537 million pesos.
The company intends to open this year 40 Jollibee stores in the country which will bring the total to 248.
It had also set 30 new stores for its unit Greenwich pizza, taking the total to 110. Greenwhich is expected to contribute 10 percent to revenues and net income this year, de la Rosa said.
Overseas, some 20 new Jollibee stores have been planned for this year to total to 44. De la Rosa said these would be established in China, Hong Kong, Indonesia and possibly Thailand.
